range.description: The time window this read applied: events with `range.from` <= `timestamp` < `range.to`. Without `from`, the server uses at most the 24 hours before `to`, so compare this with the window you meant. Absent from servers older than this field.

from.description: Inclusive start the server applied (ISO 8601 UTC, milliseconds): the request's `from`, or `to` minus 24 hours when `from` was absent, never before 1900-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.

to.description: Exclusive end the server applied (ISO 8601 UTC, milliseconds): the request's `to`, or the server clock when `to` was absent, never after 2299-12-31T23:59:59.999Z.

total.description: Matching events in the whole window (every page, not only this one). A lower bound when `totalExact` is false.

totalExact.description: False when `total` is a lower bound because the server could not establish an exact count: the count stops at 10,001, failed, did not finish within its 1 second budget, or saw fewer events than this page proves. Exact means exact for `range`: events outside the window are not counted. Absent from older servers: treat as exact below 10,001.

deliveryWindowSeconds.description: Deliver an event only if it arrived no later than this many seconds after it occurred (receivedAt − occurredAt). A whole number of hours, from 1 hour to 3,650 days; null means no limit. Later events stay stored and searchable but are not delivered. Resends and test pings ignore the window. A change applies to events discovered after the save.

filterWarning.description: Discovery and delivery are paused. webhook_filter_review_required: confirm a filter stored before webhook delivery. webhook_filter_invalid: the stored filter cannot run, for example a regex that RE2 rejects. Include a valid filterQuery in an endpoint PATCH to resume from the saved cursor.

lateEvents.description: Events in this project that arrived later than this endpoint's window, before the endpoint's filter and scope are applied, recorded in the whole arrival hours from `since`: the first hour boundary at or after the later of the endpoint's last window change and 30 days ago (the delivery log retention). It counts arrivals, so it includes late events since removed by retention or deletion and can exceed what a search finds. The count is approximate: it is exact in normal operation, but after a storage failure, a retried write or a restore it can be lower or higher than the true number. There is no backfill: arrivals before the deployment added this count are not included. Do not use it for reconciliation. 0 when the window is null. null only in a PATCH response when the count could not be read: the settings were saved regardless; read the endpoint again for the count.

get.description: Search stored events in one time window, one page at a time. The window runs from `from` (inclusive) to `to` (exclusive) on the stored `timestamp`: the event's occurredAt, or the time Logbird received it when occurredAt was absent or unusable. Without `from` it is at most the 24 hours before `to` (the store limits, 1900-01-01T00:00:00.000Z to 2299-12-31T23:59:59.999Z, can shorten it); without `to` it ends at the server clock. The response states the window it applied as `range`: a history read here is complete only for that window, whatever `totalExact` says. Events sort by `timestamp`, then by event `id` in the same direction (`order`). Events in the same millisecond are ordered by id, not by cause: read causation from `context.parentEventId`. Follow `nextCursor` until it is null, sending the same `q` and `order`, and the first page's `range` as `from` and `to` (a cursor carries no window, so omitted bounds would be resolved again on every page), and use absolute times in `q`: a relative time (`receivedAt:>now-1h`) is read against each request's clock and can drop an event between pages. Each page continues after the previous page's last event. Fixed bounds keep the window, not the events: the pass is still not a snapshot. Paging is not a snapshot: an event stored after you started, with a `timestamp` behind your position, is not on the later pages. `receivedAt:` in `q` helps find late arrivals, with a `from` early enough to cover when they can have occurred (the window still filters on `timestamp`). Receipt times are not a strict sequence: events can share a millisecond, and an event recovered after a storage failure keeps its original receipt time. So re-read with a generous overlap (`receivedAt:>=` a time well before the last one you saw) and drop ids you already have; an overlap narrows the gap but cannot prove it closed. `total` counts the whole window (a lower bound when `totalExact` is false). A scoped key or viewer token sees only its scope, and `q` cannot widen it.

Send an ISO 8601 date-time in UTC (Z) or with an offset, read to the millisecond: a date-time without an offset is read in the server's time zone, and a date alone is midnight UTC. get.description: How far back this caller's history reaches. `oldestEventAt` is the `timestamp` of the oldest event this caller can find through search: the first event that an `order=asc` search over the widest window (`from` 1900-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, `to` 2299-12-31T23:59:59.999Z, exclusive) returns to the same caller, within its scope for a scoped key or viewer token, or null when that search finds none. It describes what is stored now, not what ever existed: an empty history before it does not prove that nothing happened then. `retentionDays` is the project's retention policy, the same for every reader of the project, and the one value here that a scoped caller could not already find. Each retention run (hourly, and right after the window is shortened) deletes for good the events dated more than that many days before the run. Between runs, older events can still be stored and found, for example one that arrived dated in the past, so `oldestEventAt` can lie before now minus `retentionDays`, and it can move back as well as forward. Raising `retentionDays` restores nothing. To read a whole history, search from `oldestEventAt` to a `to` later than any stored event: an event can be dated up to one day after it was received, so use a `to` more than a day after now (for example two days).

schema.description: How far back the caller can read. To read a whole history, search from `oldestEventAt` to a `to` more than a day after now (an event can be dated up to one day after it was received), and do not take an empty answer before `oldestEventAt` as proof that nothing happened.

oldestEventAt.description: The `timestamp` of the oldest event this caller can find through search (ISO 8601 UTC, milliseconds): the first event of an `order=asc` search over the widest window, or null when that search finds none. It describes what is stored now: retention or deletion may have removed older events, raising `retentionDays` brings none back, and it can move back as well as forward (an event can arrive dated in the past).

retentionDays.description: The project's retention policy in days, the same for every reader of the project. Each retention run (hourly, and right after the window is shortened) deletes for good the events dated more than this many days before the run. Between runs, older events can still be stored and found, so this is not a bound on what a search returns.
